svg.title: Weaving draft - 2/2 twill on four shafts

g.text: A draft is not a picture of cloth. It is the instruction.
Three small grids decide the fourth: threading, tie-up, treadling.
So weavers exchange drafts, not swatches - a draft can be run again.
The drawdown here was computed from the other three, not drawn by hand.
FOUR GRIDS, AND ONE OF THEM IS THE ANSWER
HOW A SQUARE IS FILLED IN
CHANGE ONE GRID, GET ANOTHER CLOTH
which shaft each warp end passes
the order the treadles are pressed
is not drawn - it is worked out
read the treadle from the treadling
the tie-up says which shafts lift
the threading says which ends are on them
are on top, so their squares are filled
1 2 3 4, so the line runs one way
a draft is written, not the cloth
looms were the first programmed machines
THREADING - which shaft each warp end goes on
